slot.brief: Which of the given orderings across electronegativity, electron gain enthalpy and ionisation enthalpy (including anomalies like Cl > F, O vs S) is incorrect?

stem: Which ordering is incorrect? In the electron-gain ordering, greater means more energy released on adding an electron; IE denotes first ionisation enthalpy.

verdicts.working: Pauling electronegativities give F > O > Cl > N, so (A) is correct and (D) is incorrect. Electron-gain energies follow Cl > F > S > O, and first ionisation enthalpies follow N > O > P > S; (B) and (C) are correct.

working:
Electronegativity: $	ext{F}>	ext{O}>	ext{Cl}>	ext{N}$.
Energy released on electron gain: $	ext{Cl}>	ext{F}>	ext{S}>	ext{O}$.
First IE: $	ext{N}>	ext{O}>	ext{P}>	ext{S}$.
Thus A–C are correct; D incorrectly places Cl above F in electronegativity.

Independent check: Pauling electronegativities give F > O > Cl > N, so (A) is correct and (D) is incorrect. Electron-gain energies follow Cl > F > S > O, and first ionisation enthalpies follow N > O > P > S; (B) and (C) are correct.
solution:
Electronegativity decreases as $\text{F}>\text{O}>\text{Cl}>\text{N}$.
Thus the ordering $\text{Cl}>\text{F}>\text{O}>\text{N}$ is incorrect.
